title: Illinois's 5th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: The general election for Illinois's 5th Congressional District pits 16-year Democratic incumbent Mike Quigley against Republican challenger Tommy Hanson in what has become a recurring rematch. The district covers Chicago's North Side and nearby suburbs in Cook and Lake counties and has a Cook Partisan Voting Index of D+19, making it one of the most reliably Democratic seats in Illinois. Quigley, who has held the seat since a 2009 special election, has defeated Hanson in each of the last four general elections by margins ranging from 69% to 76%. The race is rated 'Solid D' by the Cook Political Report, though Hanson continues to campaign on fiscal conservatism, crime reduction, and alignment with President Donald Trump.
polling_note: No independent general election polls were found for this race as of June 2026. The district is considered safely Democratic.

candidates.name: Mike Quigley
candidates.summary: Mike Quigley is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Illinois's 5th Congressional District, first elected in a 2009 special election following Rahm Emanuel's resignation. He previously served as a Cook County Commissioner and has built a reputation as a fiscally responsible, socially liberal Democrat who serves on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and the Appropriations Subcommittee on Transportation, Housing, and Urban Development. Quigley also founded the bipartisan Congressional Transparency Caucus and has been a leading voice in support of Ukraine and LGBTQ+ rights.

candidates.name: Tom Hanson
candidates.summary: Tom Hanson, who also goes by Tommy Hanson, is the Republican nominee for Illinois's 5th Congressional District and a commercial real estate broker from Chicago. He has been the Republican challenger to Mike Quigley in the last four consecutive general elections, running on a platform of fiscal conservatism, reducing federal spending, and supporting law enforcement. Hanson describes himself as a 'common-sense conservative' and a 'Liberal Republican' who is fiscally conservative and socially liberal, and he has campaigned on proposals such as replacing individual income taxes with tariffs and a fair tax system.
